facts.fact: A referral code is not required to start Valhalla.
facts.answer_guidance: Tell the user to run /valhalla start or use the Valhalla website.

facts.fact: Users can start with /valhalla start, then use /valhalla settings_dlmm to configure copy trading.
facts.answer_guidance: Keep setup instructions short; ask whether they are using Discord or the website if the path is unclear.

facts.fact: The official Valhalla Getting Started guide (https://valhalla-bot.gitbook.io/valhalla-bot/getting-started) is the approved setup walkthrough: run /valhalla start, then /valhalla settings_dlmm, choose Follow Wallet, and select Turn On. The same setup is available from the Valhalla website at https://valhalla-bot.app/.
facts.answer_guidance: If someone asks for a setup video or tutorial and no verified video link is available, say that you do not have a verified Valhalla video link to share and give this official guide and setup flow instead. Do not invent or guess a video URL.

facts.fact: When a user asks how much Valhalla charges, link the official Valhalla fees FAQ.
facts.answer_guidance: Use https://valhalla-bot.gitbook.io/valhalla-bot/valhalla-faq. Do not mix in old buy/sell fee wording from older pages.

facts.fact: A Decoder NFT or subscription is not required to start or use Valhalla. They provide fee discounts and unlock full access to premium Discord channels; without them, base functionality remains available.
facts.answer_guidance: Answer directly when asked about NFT or subscription requirements. Do not say either is mandatory to start. Do not state a subscription price unless it is separately verified.

facts.fact: Valhalla does not require an API key to set up or use its documented Discord flows.
facts.answer_guidance: Tell users to use /valhalla start and the documented setup commands. Never ask them to paste an API key or direct them to an obsolete third-party key provider.

facts.fact: Valhalla charges a 0.015% opening fee and a 3% claim fee on Meteora fees earned.
facts.answer_guidance: Prefer linking the fees FAQ instead of explaining the rates unless the user asks for the specific breakdown.

facts.fact: Valhalla copies supported Meteora DLMM activity from followed wallets; a normal token buy is not a DLMM position.
facts.answer_guidance: If a specific trade did not copy, escalate rather than guessing about the user's position.

facts.fact: Valhalla's documented hard cap is 50 open positions, while users can also configure a per-wallet position count and timeframe.
facts.answer_guidance: Do not promise that a user's configured limit is the only limit; specific skipped positions require investigation.

facts.fact: Valhalla results vary with the wallets followed, the user's ratio and filters, liquidity, and market conditions; staff must not promise profit.
facts.answer_guidance: Point users to the Valhalla wallets channel and /valhalla top_trade_wallets for current examples, while stating that past performance is not a guarantee.

facts.fact: DAMM v2 copying is in beta and can have bugs; users testing it should use an amount they are comfortable risking and specific issues should be escalated.
facts.answer_guidance: Do not describe DAMM as fully stable or guarantee that a test will work.

facts.fact: A missed or differing Valhalla copy can involve skipped positions, timing, filters, liquidity, or execution state; the bot cannot identify the cause from a message alone.
facts.answer_guidance: Ask for the safe webhook or position context and route a specific discrepancy to a human; never invent a cause.

facts.fact: Valhalla can be started from the website at https://valhalla-bot.app/ as an alternative to the Discord command flow.
facts.answer_guidance: Point users to the official site or /valhalla start; do not ask for wallet keys or credentials.

source.ref: older onboarding replies and inspected screenshots 2026-09-08

facts.fact: The copy ratio is intended to make the follower risk a similar proportion of their wallet as the followed trader risks of theirs. For example, if the followed trader risks 10% of their wallet per position, a matching ratio is intended to make the follower risk about 10% of their own wallet per position.
facts.answer_guidance: Explain the proportion first and use the 10% example when the user asks how to size the ratio. This describes proportional sizing; do not promise profit, safety, or recommend a personal risk level.

source.ref: holder-chat staff reply, 2026-09-07: trader risking 10% of wallet per position should be matched proportionally

facts.fact: Entry Mode supports SOL_ONLY, SOL_OR_USDC, and ANY, with safety rails able to clamp the effective mode to SOL_ONLY.
facts.answer_guidance: Explain tradeoffs without telling the user which mode will make money. A specific unexpected skip is an escalation.

facts.fact: When the Jupiter score is 30 or lower, Pumpfun and StonkFun-only behavior is automatically enforced as a safety measure, subject to configured exemptions.
facts.answer_guidance: Do not describe the safety rail as a guarantee or advise bypassing it.

facts.fact: To set the minimum Jupiter score to 0, open Wallet Settings → Advanced Settings → Filters in Valhalla, then set Min Jup Score to 0. The same setting is available from the Valhalla website as well as the Discord settings flow.
facts.answer_guidance: Give the exact navigation path when asked about Jup 0. Do not describe disabling the score as a safety guarantee or recommend bypassing other safety restrictions.

source.ref: user clarification 2026-09-10; verified Valhalla settings UI path

facts.fact: Questions about private keys, PIN recovery, missing funds, withdrawals, or suspected wallet compromise must go to a human.
facts.answer_guidance: Never request or repeat a seed phrase, private key, or access token.

facts.fact: Specific Valhalla positions, balances, PnL, failed or duplicated copies, withdrawals, and unexpected funds require human investigation.
facts.answer_guidance: Ask for safe context such as the wallet display name, pool, or screenshot; never ask for private keys or seed phrases.

facts.fact: Olympus is a web terminal for Polymarket manual trading, copy trading, markets, sports, perps, leverage, combos, and related workflows.
facts.answer_guidance: Use the official docs for feature-specific instructions.

facts.fact: Users sign in to Olympus on the website with Discord or Gmail through Privy, then fund the trading wallet and optionally follow a wallet.
facts.answer_guidance: Link the official getting-started guide for a full walkthrough.

facts.fact: Imported wallet flows are available in Olympus.
facts.answer_guidance: Do not assume an imported wallet has the same Safe or gasless setup as an Olympus-created wallet; inspect the account-specific wallet type and escalate when needed.

facts.fact: Olympus-created Deposit Wallets are gasless for supported trading flows, while legacy Safe or EOA setups can have different gas requirements; imported wallets must be checked by wallet type.
facts.answer_guidance: Explain the distinction without promising that a particular user's wallet is gasless; ask which wallet type or request safe account context when necessary.

source.ref: older Olympus wallet support replies and inspected screenshots 2026-09-08

facts.fact: An Olympus account can show a signer EOA and a separate trading/funder address. The signer EOA authorizes relayer batches and CLOB orders and does not hold trading funds after provisioning. The trading/funder address holds funds and positions; for the default walletType=deposit, it is the deposit wallet address, while legacy Safe/proxy wallets use their Safe address.
facts.answer_guidance: Explain that the signing address authorizes actions and the deposit/trading wallet holds funds and positions. For a new default Deposit Wallet, the trading address is the deposit wallet address. Do not turn this general explanation into an account investigation unless the user says their displayed addresses or funds do not match.

facts.fact: Olympus detects a followed leader's activity and attempts to mirror it using the follower's ratio, size limits, filters, and execution mode.
facts.answer_guidance: A specific missing, duplicated, incorrectly sized, or unexpectedly filled trade must be escalated.

facts.fact: Max Trade Size (USD) is the maximum amount Olympus will use for one copied trade. When the amount calculated from the follower's ratio is higher than this setting, Olympus caps that individual copied trade at the Max Trade Size.
facts.answer_guidance: Distinguish this from Max Market Size, which caps the total capital deployed into one market for that wallet. Do not diagnose a user's specific order size; escalate a missing, incorrectly sized, or unexpected copied trade.

facts.fact: Backtesting is a simulation of a trader's history against the user's settings, not a guarantee of future copied results.
facts.answer_guidance: Mention modeled fills and the user's own settings when relevant; never promise profitability.

facts.fact: Olympus provides a leaderboard, top-wallet views, and per-trader pages where users can inspect potential leaders before following them.
facts.answer_guidance: Point users to the Olympus leaderboard or top-wallet views. Do not present any leader as guaranteed profitable; performance depends on the leader and the user's settings.

source.ref: olympus-main 5 frontend leaderboard, top-wallet, and per-trader flows

facts.fact: In Olympus order status, Copied indicates a fully filled order, Limit Placed indicates an order waiting for fill, and Partial Fill indicates that only part of the order filled.
facts.answer_guidance: Explain status labels without claiming a specific user's order filled; account-specific discrepancies require human review.

facts.fact: Unexpected leftover shares, slippage, skipped sells, failed copies, or mismatches between a leader and follower require investigation with the relevant webhook, order, or account context.
facts.answer_guidance: Ask for safe screenshots, order IDs, market links, or webhook details; do not promise a root cause or outcome.

source.ref: older Olympus ticket and holder-chat replies 2026-09-08

facts.fact: Olympus fee questions should be answered from the official FAQ and the dedicated feature fee schedule when applicable.
facts.answer_guidance: Do not infer a fee from a screenshot or from a different product's fee schedule.

facts.fact: Olympus does not guarantee profitability; results depend on the followed wallet, settings, fills, fees, liquidity, and market conditions.
facts.answer_guidance: Explain the risk plainly and point to backtesting or wallet activity without presenting simulated or historical results as a promise.

facts.fact: Sports markets are accessed from the Sports area; users can search or open Game View and use the market dropdown to select a market such as Moneyline.
facts.answer_guidance: If markets or outcomes are missing for a specific event, collect the event details and escalate to the product team.

source.ref: ticket-4057 staff replies and inspected screenshots

facts.fact: Dimes is an external integration that powers Olympus leverage-related behavior; specific leverage, closing, or payout discrepancies require human investigation.
facts.answer_guidance: Do not claim Olympus controls Dimes' closing logic or guarantee a user's funds or outcome.

facts.fact: Specific balances, positions, PnL, redemptions, withdrawals, missing funds, and trade discrepancies must be handled by a human with account context.
facts.answer_guidance: Ask only for safe, non-secret identifiers or screenshots; never ask for private keys or seed phrases.

source.ref: Olympus ticket-4019, ticket-4040, and ticket-4059 patterns

facts.fact: In Olympus, Redeemed means a position in a resolved market has been claimed or settled. For winning shares, this converts the shares back into USDC.
facts.answer_guidance: Use this only for a general definition. A user's missing, stuck, pending, failed, or incorrect redemption remains an account-specific escalation.

source.ref: Olympus general staff reply 1535011277150359612, cross-checked against the current redeem event implementation

facts.fact: After starting Valhalla, users enable copy trading in /valhalla settings_dlmm by choosing Follow Wallet and then Turn On.
facts.answer_guidance: Give these two setup actions when someone asks how to begin copying a wallet. Do not add unrelated settings unless asked.

facts.fact: Valhalla lets each followed wallet have its own take-profit and stop-loss settings, position count and timeframe limits, and minimum token age, market-cap, holder-count, and trade-volume filters.
facts.answer_guidance: Explain which filter the user asked about. Do not recommend a personal value or imply any setting guarantees profit.

facts.fact: Valhalla does not copy liquidity adds to an already existing position, claims below $2, manually opened DLMM positions, or positions beyond the 50-open-position cap; supported pools are SOL and USDC pools.
facts.answer_guidance: Use this for general questions about what will not copy. A specific missed trade still needs account and transaction context before its cause can be identified.

facts.fact: Valhalla positions live on Meteora; users need to export the Valhalla wallet before viewing that wallet's positions in Phantom.
facts.answer_guidance: Never ask a user to post exported keys. For a specific missing position or wallet issue, route it for investigation.

facts.fact: A position opened directly on Meteora outside Valhalla is untracked and shown read-only; Valhalla does not manage it as a copied position.
facts.answer_guidance: Correct the meaning of read-only without claiming anything about a user's specific position.

facts.fact: Valhalla position PnL is calculated as current value plus fees earned minus deposited amount; claimed fees belong in fees earned and are not counted again in current value.
facts.answer_guidance: Explain the formula generally. Do not calculate or confirm a user's actual PnL without account data.

facts.fact: Valhalla's Max per Token setting is a per-user ceiling on cumulative SOL deposited into one token across the user's open positions, not a separate cap for each followed wallet.
facts.answer_guidance: Explain the scope of the ceiling. Do not recommend a value or promise that it prevents all loss.

facts.fact: Olympus Ask AI can search markets, read trading information, summarize a portfolio, and propose an order, but it does not place an order without the user clicking Confirm.
facts.answer_guidance: State the confirmation requirement directly. A report that an order happened without confirmation is account-specific and must be escalated.

source.ref: Olympus product notes and support history indexed 2026-09-09

facts.fact: An Olympus combo is a multi-leg parlay position: several market outcomes are bundled together and every leg must settle successfully for the combined position to pay.
facts.answer_guidance: Do not describe a combo as a simple basket of independent trades.

facts.fact: Olympus perps are leveraged perpetual futures settled in pUSD and do not expire; the supported instruments are SP500, GOLD, WTIOIL, NAS100, SILVER, and BTC.
facts.answer_guidance: Describe the feature without recommending leverage, margin, direction, or an instrument.

source.ref: Olympus product notes and leverage replies indexed 2026-09-09

facts.fact: Olympus Perps Automation currently executes RSI rules on closed candles; MACD Crossover, EMA Golden Cross, and Bollinger Band Touch are displayed as placeholders and do not fire trades.
facts.answer_guidance: Explain the implementation boundary. Do not recommend RSI bands or suggest that automation will make money.

facts.fact: Perps Automation can skip a trigger when the instrument already has an open position; rules on one instrument must use the same direction because perps net exposure per instrument.
facts.answer_guidance: Use this for general questions about a rule not firing. A specific account trigger still needs logs and account context.

facts.fact: Polymarket can hold orders on live sports and esports markets in an in-play delay state; if the order does not clear within the allowed window, it may be treated as rejected.
facts.answer_guidance: Explain this as venue behavior, not proof that every specific order failure has this cause.

facts.fact: A Maker Copy-Buy is priced at or below the best bid, so it can rest on the order book and avoid taker fees, but it may fill late or not fill at all.
facts.answer_guidance: Describe the tradeoff without recommending maker or taker execution.

facts.fact: Olympus copy-trade fees are recorded as trades execute and collected in a daily on-chain sweep rather than as a separate charge beside every fill; the normal trade fee is 0.75% base or 0.20% reduced, while LP fill fees are 0.2% on both legs.
facts.answer_guidance: Link the official fee schedule for current details. Do not infer a fee from a screenshot or apply Olympus rates to Valhalla.

facts.fact: A verified deposit of at least $50 into a newly created Olympus trading wallet within seven days raises the user's referral commission from 25% to 30%; it is not a trading-fee discount or a zero-fee period.
facts.answer_guidance: Answer the bonus mechanics only when asked. Do not promise eligibility for a specific account without account context.

facts.fact: Olympus's failsafe compares on-chain follower holdings with copy-trading records; a Stray is attributed to a leader who has sold, while an Orphan has no attribution record.
facts.answer_guidance: Define the terms generally. Specific positions or automatic closures require human investigation.

facts.fact: Valhalla wallet discovery is available in the Valhalla wallets channel and through /valhalla top_trade_wallets.
facts.answer_guidance: Point users to the channel name and command for current examples, while making clear that historical performance is not a guarantee.
